messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@orionhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@orionhealth.com
Date: Sun, 1 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form Qs — auto-renew / termination for convenience

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the draft order form. Procurement has flagged two items that are blocking internal approval: the auto-renew window (currently 90 days) and the Termination for Convenience pricing exposure. Their ask is: reduce notice to 60 days and add a short termination-for-convenience fee to cover committed provisioning costs if we exit mid-term.

I've attached our redline (Orion_Health_OrderForm_Redline_20250601.docx). Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept 60-day opt-out and whether you can propose a narrow TFc fee (e.g., pro rata for remaining prepaid months or a flat 20% of remaining committed ARR)? We need a response for the exec procurement committee next week (they meet on 6/8).

Thanks — hope we can find middle ground.

Best,
Alicia Gomez
VP, Procurement
Orion Health

Attachments: Orion_Health_OrderForm_Redline_20250601.docx (redline)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form Qs — auto-renew / termination for convenience

Alicia — thanks for the redline and the heads-up on timing. Looping in Ben (sales lead) and Marissa (legal lead) to coordinate a concise counterproposal.

Short summary of what we can/should propose:
- Opt-out / Auto-renew: willing to move from 90 -> 60 days if we keep the remainder of the term billing intact and include an explicit reminder cadence (30/45 days) in the order form. This preserves predictable capacity planning for Dedicated customers.
- Termination for Convenience (TFC): we prefer to avoid open-ended TFc fees. Proposed compromise: customer may terminate for convenience with 60 days' notice and a termination fee equal to the lesser of (a) 3 months of remaining committed Monthly Recurring Charge (MRC) or (b) 20% of remaining committed ARR. This limits exposure while giving a clear remedy.

Ben / Marissa — can you review and confirm legal's comfort with the draft language below? If ok, I'll send back to Alicia with a tracked Order Form and a short summary for procurement. We should also prepare a fallback: if procurement insists on no fee, require 90-day notice.

DRAFT LANGUAGE (for order form):
"Termination for Convenience: Either party may terminate this Order Form for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice to the other party. If Customer terminates for convenience during the term, Customer shall pay to Redwood, as a termination fee, the lesser of (i) three (3) months of Customer's remaining Monthly Recurring Charges under the Order Form, or (ii) twenty percent (20%) of the remaining committed Annual Recurring Revenue for the then-current Term."

I will attach a marked-up Order Form if you both sign off.

Irene Choi
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: RI_Draft_OrderForm_60day_redline.docx (will attach after internal ok)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 3 Jun 2025 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form Qs — auto-renew / termination for convenience

Irene — agreed on the approach; Marissa can confirm legal tweak but this is commercially reasonable and preserves our cost model. A couple notes:

1) Reminder cadence: add two automated reminders (30 and 45 days before renewal) and an explicit statement that notices must be sent to contracts@redwood.ai to be effective.
2) TFc fee: prefer the "lesser of" construction to cap exposure. Suggest we add a carve-out that excludes any prepaid non-refundable onboarding fees from the calculation so we don't double-dip.

Updated draft snippet (for legal redline):
"If Customer provides notice under this Section, Customer shall pay the lesser of (i) three (3) months of Customer's remaining Monthly Recurring Charges under the Order Form, excluding any non-refundable onboarding or professional services fees, or (ii) twenty percent (20%) of the remaining committed Annual Recurring Revenue for the then-current Term."

Marissa — if legal is comfortable with the carve-out and the requirement that notices be sent to contracts@redwood.ai, happy to send to Alicia by EOD.

-Ben

Ben Carter
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
